newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese wine output seen up to 30 percent lower.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese wine output seen up to 30 percent lower.

text.p: Portugal's wine production is expected to drop by up to 30 percent this year from bumper levels in 1996 because of unfavourable weather, a senior industry official said on Wednesday.
"I expect that production will drop by 20 to 30 percent this year because of abnormal weather conditions so far this year," Jose Soeiro, president of the Wine and Vineyard Institute, told Reuters.
Wine production in 1996 was about 9.5 million hectolitres, of which some 1.8 million hectolitres were exported, mainly to the resf of the European Union and Scandinavia.
Portugal had an unusually dry spring and wet early summer, which hit grape production.
The worst hit regions were the Dao and Douro regions of northern Portugal, where young wine, or "vinho verde", is cultivated, Soeiro said.

Production of port wine was expected to be little changed because farmers diverted grapes to the more profitable port production from other types of wine in difficult years, said Cristina Mello, economist at the Port Wine Institute in Oporto in northern Portugal.

She said stocks of grapes were at comfortable levels and port production this year should come close to the 165,000 "pipes" produced in 1996, a normal year in terms of port wine output. Each pipe measures 550 litres.
